title: Therapeutic potential of glycyrrhizic acid in inflammation-related diseases: from HMGB1-oriented molecular insights to preclinical application.
authors: Hu, Yicheng; Hou, Jiani; Cai, Yifeng; Ni, Chaoran; Xing, Zhewen; Li, Jingtian; Zhou, Zan; Xu, Guangtao; Zeng, Xiansi; Jia, Jinjing; Li, Li
one_liner_zh: 综述甘草酸抗炎机制，涉及HMGB1蛋白与配体分子对接，但核心是炎症信号通路与临床转化，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Chronic inflammation drives the pathogenesis of diverse disorders, yet current anti-inflammatory strategies often lack mechanistic selectivity. Glycyrrhizic acid (GL), a major triterpenoid saponin from Glycyrrhiza species, exhibits broad anti-inflammatory effects, but its mechanism has been viewed as non-specific. In this review, we propose an integrated framework positioning high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) as one major molecular hub for GL's action. Mechanistically, our molecular docking analysis suggests that GL may interact with the Box B domain of HMGB1 andmay potentially interfere with its engagement with TLR4 and RAGE, thereby orchestrating a cascade inhibition of downstream NF-kappaB, MAPK, and NLRP3 inflammasome pathways. Beyond this core signaling axis, we systematically analyze how GL context-dependently modulates macrophage polarization, monocyte-derived macrophage differentiation, and Th17/Treg balance. We further synthesize its effects across liver, autoimmune, metabolic, oncologic, neurological, and renal diseases, revealing shared mechanisms and disease-specific adaptations. Finally, we critically evaluate translational bottlenecks-including isomer-specific bioavailability, the pseudoaldosteronism risk, and formulation challenges-and propose strategies to overcome them. By shifting from a descriptive summary to a mechanism-centered, integrative analysis, this review provides a conceptual framework for developing GL as a multitarget anti-inflammatory agent, while acknowledging its limitations including low oral bioavailability, microbiota-dependent metabolism, pseudoaldosteronism risk, and limited clinical evidence.
abstract_zh: 慢性炎症驱动多种疾病的发病机制，然而当前的抗炎策略往往缺乏机制选择性。甘草酸（GL），一种来自甘草属植物的主要三萜皂苷，表现出广泛的抗炎作用，但其机制一直被视为非特异性。在本综述中，我们提出一个整合框架，将高迁移率族蛋白B1（HMGB1）定位为GL作用的一个主要分子枢纽。在机制层面，我们的分子对接分析提示，GL可能与HMGB1的Box B结构域相互作用，并可能干扰其与TLR4和RAGE的结合，从而协调下游NF-kappaB、MAPK和NLRP3炎症小体通路的级联抑制。在此核心信号轴之外，我们系统分析了GL如何以情境依赖方式调节巨噬细胞极化、单核细胞来源的巨噬细胞分化以及Th17/Treg平衡。我们进一步综合了其在肝脏、自身免疫、代谢、肿瘤、神经和肾脏疾病中的作用，揭示了共享机制和疾病特异性适应。最后，我们批判性评估了转化瓶颈——包括异构体特异性生物利用度、假性醛固酮增多症风险以及制剂挑战——并提出了克服这些障碍的策略。通过从描述性总结转向以机制为中心的整合分析，本综述为开发GL作为多靶点抗炎药物提供了概念框架，同时承认其局限性，包括低口服生物利用度、微生物群依赖性代谢、假性醛固酮增多症风险以及有限的临床证据。
